key_insight: A probabilistic deep-learning pipeline can forecast phase transformation in steel from in situ microscopy and thermal history by jointly learning image features, temperature dynamics, and uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, data-driven prediction of microstructure evolution during heat treatment, supporting process design for new alloys where classical transformation diagrams are unavailable.
method: Beta-variational autoencoder compresses the initial microscopy image into a low-dimensional latent state.
Temporal Fusion Transformer uses the latent image features plus cooling rate and full temperature history to predict Widmanstatten ferrite ratio quantiles.
Gaussian process corrects the end-state equilibrium level and produces probabilistic prediction intervals.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on Widmanstatten ferrite evolution in S235 steel across five cooling regimes and reported significant accuracy.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of in situ microscopy data and may require retraining or recalibration for other alloys and thermal schedules.
paper_title: Probabilistic Deep Learning Framework for Phase Transformation Forecasting aided by In Situ High temperature Microscopy
